catalog.summary: Preview card that opens on hover or focus.

patternStatus: The APG has no hover-card pattern. Its tooltip page names the non-modal dialog for hover content that contains focusable elements, which is what the panel is when navigable; WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.13 states what the card owes a reader — Dismissible, Hoverable, Persistent — and each of the three is answered in dismissal below. Both were read on 2026-09-16.

roles.root: the trigger's own — a link, or whatever render gives
roles.content: dialog when navigable, presentation when not

rolesReason: A card the keyboard can enter is the APG's non-modal dialog. A card it cannot enter is not a dialog, and a dialog nothing points to is what Radix ships; Base UI keeps the link as the only accessible interface and the card out of the way. The panel's role follows navigable, and the trigger says aria-haspopup="dialog" only when that is true.
holdsReason: The card is popover unchanged behind a hover trigger, as menubar holds menu and context-menu holds menu. popover declined opening on hover to this family (tooltip-and-popover inventory l. 116) so that two families would not answer one question; this family answers it by owning the trigger and overriding two of the popover's defaults (overrides below), and re-exports none of the panel's parts. The cost is one context, paid in popover once: the panel has to let the consumer's role win.

autoFocus.reason: A card that took focus from the link under the pointer would be a dialog wearing the wrong trigger.

sideOffset.reason: The arrow's tip stands one pixel off the anchor's box, which is right for a button and wrong for a word: the open mark's halo reaches two pixels past the link's box, and the tip touched it. The offset is the halo (--slotted-space-1) plus the same again of air, and a consumer may still set the popover's own sideOffset.

composesReason: Every overlay module reaches the family through popover. pointer-intent is the family's own: the grace area on the way from the trigger to the card, written for menu's submenu and promised to this family in menu's design §5.
rootReason: Radix and Base UI both render the <a> themselves and take a substitute through asChild or render. The trigger is the one element the family paints — the link while its card is showing — and rendering it onto another family's root keeps that root's identity, because the other family's props are spread after this one's.

openDelay.reason: The number tooltip holds and the one Base UI reached; Radix uses 700. Two hover-opened families with two warmups would read as two libraries.

closeDelay.reason: Radix and Base UI both use 300. Twice the tooltip's, because a card is farther from its trigger and larger than a hint, and the grace area below covers the travel while this covers the pause.

focus.reason: Focus opens the card in the same task, as tooltip decided: a delay a reader cannot shorten by moving faster is a delay for nothing. Only :focus-visible opens it — a press that focuses a link is a navigation.

grace.effect: the card stays open while the pointer's own path from the trigger still points into the card's rectangle; the grace ends when the path turns away or after closeDelay with no movement
grace.reason: Radix and Ark rely on closeDelay alone, so a pointer that crosses a paragraph on the diagonal loses the card. The rectangle is the layer's as positioner resolved it, so a card that flipped gets a grace area on the side it landed on.

pointerLeave.effect: closes after closeDelay once the pointer is off both the trigger and the card, and the grace area no longer holds

blur.effect: focus leaves the trigger and does not enter the card

escape.effect: the topmost layer only; focus stays or returns to the trigger, which does not reopen — Dismissible

outsidePress.effect: a press outside the layer and its branches

guard.effect: focus reached a focus guard past either end of the card; focus returns to the trigger, which does not reopen

close.effect: the popover's Close part, the target a touch reader has when there is no Escape key

dismissal.hoverable: the pointer may move onto the card and the card stays — Hoverable
dismissal.persistent: the card stays until hover and focus have left both trigger and card, until Escape, or until the consumer closes it — Persistent

reopen.rule: focus the family itself puts back on the trigger holds the reopening back until focus leaves the trigger once
reopen.reason: Without it a guard closes the card, focuses the trigger, and the trigger opens the card again: a loop the reader cannot leave.

touch.openTrigger: a tap on the trigger while the card is open follows the link
touch.reason: There is no hover on a coarse pointer. Radix ships nothing for touch and Base UI declares the card not touch navigable; docs/process/build-order.md decides that touch opens by click. The cost is one extra tap to navigate, stated on the reference page beside the alternative, which is a preview no touch reader can ever see.

navigable.off: the field's behaviour: the card is not keyboard-reachable, its role is presentation, and the trigger carries no aria-haspopup
navigable.on: Tab on the open trigger moves focus into the card's first tabbable; the popover's focus guards return focus to the trigger past either end; the panel is role="dialog", named by its title, and the trigger carries aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-expanded and aria-controls
navigable.reason: Radix says the content is inaccessible to keyboard users and Base UI says it is not keyboard navigable. docs/process/build-order.md asks for optional navigable content, and popover already answers what Tab does at the end of a portalled non-modal layer.

keyboard.effect: on the open trigger with navigable, moves into the card's first tabbable; otherwise moves on, and the card closes with blur
keyboard.focus: the card's first tabbable, or the next element in the page

keyboard.effect: moves back; a card opened by focus closes with blur
keyboard.focus: the previous element in the page
unchanged when on the trigger; back to the trigger when inside the card

keyboard.effect: follows the link, which is the trigger's own

focus.onOpen: not taken: autoFocus is forced off, so the reader's focus stays on the link under the pointer
focus.guardsReason: The popover's two sentinels, inherited. Focus reaching one closes the card and returns to the trigger, from which the reader's next Tab continues down the page.
focus.restore: the trigger, when focus was inside the card; nothing moves otherwise

wiring.data-open: on the root while the card shows
wiring.aria-haspopup: dialog, on the root, only when navigable
wiring.aria-expanded: on the root, only when navigable
wiring.aria-controls: the panel, on the root, only when navigable
wiring.role: dialog on the panel when navigable, presentation when not

sharedCard.rule: many triggers inside one card: the trigger that starts an opening registers itself as the anchor
sharedCard.payload: onOpenChange receives the request; request.event.currentTarget is the trigger, and the consumer reads its data attributes
sharedCard.reason: Base UI 1.8 ships handle and payload for one popup shared by many triggers. Here the composition needs no API: a list of two hundred mentions mounts one card, and the request already carries the event.

popoverApi.reason: Side, align, offsets, arrow, size, width, mount, strategy, portal, collision and the panel's parts are popover's and are imported from it. Re-exporting them here would be Radix's shape, where HoverCard.Content restates Popover.Content.

viewport.reason: Base UI's PreviewCard.Viewport cross-fades content between triggers of a shared card. It animates content the consumer owns; a consumer wanting it wraps that content in presence, and a card whose content changes while open calls reposition() on the handle.

hoverDelayOnFocus.reason: Radix and Base UI delay the focus opening as they delay the hover one. tooltip decided focus never waits, and a second answer here would be two families disagreeing about one gesture.

inlineAnchor.reason: A link that wraps onto a second line measures as the box around both lines, so the card may point at the gap between them. Floating UI's inline() answers it and positioner does not expose it; recorded in docs/process/build-order.md as a reopening of positioner rather than solved here with a second engine option.

stateModelReason: The family owns the state and renders the popover controlled, so a request the popover raises — escape, outsidePress, dismiss, the guards' keyboard — reaches the consumer through one handler with one reason vocabulary. blur is the family's own, as tooltip declares it; popover does not emit it.
statesReason: The root is a link, and the family paints it only when it is the family's own <a>: accent text with a subtle underline that fills on hover and while open, and while open a tint of the accent surface drawn with a spread shadow so the inline box grows without moving a line. focus-visible is the foundation ring. There is no disabled state on the root: disabled means the card never opens, and the link still navigates.
